sections.title: Same prompt, different rolls
paragraphs: Imagine rolling dice to finish a sentence. A loaded die always lands on the same word; a fair die gives different endings each time. {{largeLanguageModel}}s sample the next {{token}} the same way — the prompt is fixed, but the path through possible words can vary.

{{temperature}} controls how adventurous that sampling is. Near zero, the {{model}} almost always picks the highest-probability wording. Higher {{temperature}} lets less likely phrases appear — creative, but harder to compare fairly.
That matters the moment you run an {{evaluation}}. If Model A wins on run 1 and Model B wins on run 2 with the same {{prompt}}, you may be measuring randomness — not quality.
Providers also expose {{topP}} (nucleus sampling) and {{maxTokens}} caps. Together they shape length and variety. Evaluation teams record these settings beside every run so results are reproducible.
Next: the knobs you should lock before comparing answers.
bullets: {{topP}} — limits which next tokens are even considered.

check.prompt: You compare two {{model}}s on the same {{prompt}}. Model A uses {{temperature}} 0; Model B uses {{temperature}} 0.9. A teammate says the winner is obvious after one run. What is the risk?
check.answer: High temperature adds randomness so one run may not reflect true quality
choices: No risk — temperature only affects speed.
High temperature adds randomness so one run may not reflect true quality
Low temperature always produces wrong answers
check.explanation: High {{temperature}} makes answers vary run to run. Fair comparison needs matched sampling settings and often multiple runs or temperature 0 for stability.

sections.title: Knobs that matter for evals
paragraphs: {{maxTokens}} prevents runaway essays — but set it too low and answers truncate mid-thought. When scoring completeness, a truncated answer loses points for a setting problem, not model quality.
{{topP}} works with {{temperature}}: even at moderate temperature, a low {{topP}} keeps word choice focused. Teams often fix both when they need stable regression checks.
Click each scenario to see which setting likely caused the behavior. Notice that "better" is meaningless if generation settings differ between contestants.
In AiEval, document provider defaults in your notes. If one {{model}} ignores temperature (some APIs treat 0 and 0.1 similarly), say so when you interpret scores.

reveals.prompt: Same prompt, answers differ wildly between runs of one {{model}}.
reveals.reveal: Likely high {{temperature}} or high {{topP}} — increase repeatability by lowering them.

reveals.prompt: Answers stop mid-sentence with no error.
reveals.reveal: Check {{maxTokens}} — the cap may be shorter than the task needs.

reveals.prompt: Two {{model}}s compared; one always writes twice as long.
reveals.reveal: Compare {{maxTokens}} and {{prompt}} length instructions — may be settings, not capability.

aside.title: Try in AiEval
aside.body: Create one {{evaluation}} and run automation twice. Note whether scores shift when generation settings differ between {{model}}s.

check.prompt: Your regression suite needs stable scores week to week. Which setting pair is the best starting point?
check.answer: Low temperature and documented max tokens
choices: High temperature and no max tokens
Low temperature and documented max tokens
Random temperature each run for variety
Max tokens set to 10 for every task
check.explanation: Low {{temperature}} reduces sampling noise; explicit {{maxTokens}} prevents length drift. Document both so {{regressionEval}} reruns stay comparable.

sections.title: Lock settings, then compare
paragraphs: Fair {{evaluation}} flow: write a clear {{prompt}}, fix generation settings, then compare {{model}}s on the same footing. Changing wording and {{temperature}} at once makes root-cause analysis impossible.
Optional practice: the Generation variance lab simulates how {{temperature}} spreads answers — a teaching shortcut, not a live API, but the lesson carries.
Next up: Comparing answers — same {{prompt}}, matched settings, measurable quality across {{model}}s.
bullets: Separate prompt changes from sampling changes when debugging.

check.prompt: In one short phrase: why lock {{temperature}} before comparing {{model}}s?
check.explanation: Matched sampling settings ensure score differences reflect {{model}} capability and {{prompt}} following — not dice-roll luck.

recapQuestions.prompt: Which knob most directly limits how long an answer can grow?
recapQuestions.explanation: {{maxTokens}} caps generated length. {{temperature}} and {{topP}} affect word choice, not the hard length ceiling.

recapQuestions.prompt: Your nightly {{regressionEval}} shows a new winner after you only changed {{temperature}}. What should you suspect first?
recapQuestions.explanation: A {{temperature}} change alters sampling — re-run with matched settings before declaring a true quality shift.
